latest_release.name: Zero Breach Toolkit 2.0.4
latest_release.body:
Zero Breach Toolkit 2.0.4. Fixes from real Mac and Windows runs. Thanks to the people testing it.

If you are on 2.0.0 to 2.0.2, please update, and if the window showed a phone as green, check it again: those versions could say more than the check had done ([2.0.3](https://github.com/interplains/Zero-Breach-Toolkit/releases/tag/v2.0.3) fixed that).

**Mac**

- **No more false "macOS is out of date" warning.** A date in a vulnerability record was being read as a version number, so every current Mac got it. Thanks to s3ba-b for finding it.
- Safari folders that macOS refuses now give the plain privacy message, and the Full Disk Access advice is left out when access is already on.

**Windows**

- **Double-clicking no longer leaves a terminal in the taskbar**, which ended the check if you closed it.
- The Quick check estimate is now 5 to 15 minutes, and connections that are closing are labelled "System" instead of "System Idle".
- Chinese, Japanese and Korean use the matching Windows font.

**Everyone**

- The report's date comparison names the AdFection campaign, rather than implying the tool looks for only one campaign.
- A check that does not apply says why in the report's detail.
- A stopped check no longer says "nothing matched" in its next steps.
- The saved report's location shows on the Result tab, and the save dialog lists file types.
- Help scrolls and fills its tab, and Japanese and Chinese wrap correctly there. Right-to-left lines leave more room in small windows.

**Your antivirus may flag these programs.** Antivirus products often wrongly flag new programs that are not code-signed yet, and some flag these. If you downloaded the file from this page, this is a false alarm and you can ignore it: the code is public, and each program has a public build record you can check. We have applied for free code signing and are reporting these false alarms to the antivirus companies. **If the file came from anywhere else, do not run it and trust the warning.**

Downloads and first-launch steps: see the [README](https://github.com/interplains/Zero-Breach-Toolkit#easiest-download-the-program-no-python-no-commands). Full list: [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/interplains/Zero-Breach-Toolkit/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

**Verify before running**

`zero-breach-toolkit.py` SHA-256: `98279a7212220260f78e72020e52420565cc6c0c00f25bb02d478902288b80fc`

Each program: `gh attestation verify <file> --repo interplains/Zero-Breach-Toolkit`. Their checksums are also GPG-signed: `gpg --verify SHA256SUMS-programs.txt.asc SHA256SUMS-programs.txt`, then `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS-programs.txt`. Signed with key `C24E C92B 12D6 670A 2516 065F 9B4D 5754 99AF A53C`.

detail.readme_excerpt:
# Zero Breach Toolkit

> **Version 2 is out:** now a double-click app for Windows, Mac and Linux, in 27 languages.
> [Download it from the latest release](https://github.com/interplains/Zero-Breach-Toolkit/releases/latest).

A free, open-source check for traces of known mercenary spyware (Pegasus, Predator,
Graphite, Candiru and others) on computers, Android phones and iPhone backups.

- **Read-only.** It does not modify source evidence or system settings. It writes only
  temporary database snapshots and the reports you ask for.
- **No network requests during a scan.** It never looks up spyware addresses and has no
  upload feature. Python network calls are blocked and redirected paths are refused. This
  is not an operating-system network sandbox; see [PRIVACY.md](PRIVACY.md).
- **States its limits.** Every report says what was found, how strong the evidence is, and
  what could not be checked. A clean result is never presented as proof that you are safe.

Made by archivegenocide. Built on [Zero Breach](https://github.com/interplains/zero-breach).

> **If you think you are being targeted right now, get expert help first.** You do not
> need to run this tool before asking. Journalists, activists, human-rights defenders and
> civil society can contact the
> [Access Now Digital Security Helpline](https://www.accessnow.org/help/) (free, 24/7,
> many languages) or [Amnesty International's Security Lab](https://securitylab.amnesty.org/get-help/).

---

## Easiest: download the program (no Python, no commands)

**You do not need to know anything technical to use this.** Download one file from the
[latest release](https://github.com/interplains/Zero-Breach-Toolkit/releases/latest), open it,
and follow the window. You do not need the source code on this page, and you do not need to
type any commands.

Once it is open: choose a check, press **Start check**, and read the result. It tells you in
plain words whether anything was found and what to do next. You can save the report if you
want to keep it or show it to someone helping you.

**Which check?** Use **Standard** unless you have a reason not to: it covers browsers, apps,
startup items, program files and out-of-date programs (usually 15 to 20 minutes). **Quick** looks
at browsers only (5 to 10 minutes). **Full** adds web caches and more file types (30 minutes or
more). You can press **Stop** at any time and keep what has been checked so far. To check a
phone, choose **A phone** in the window; the guides there explain what you need first.

**A green result is good news, not a guarantee.** It means this check found none of the published
traces it looks for, in the places it could read. It cannot find spyware nobody has published
traces of, and it does not prove a device is safe. If you think you are being targeted, ask a
digital-security helpline even if the result is green.
